skill.name: backend-api
skill.description: Design and implement RESTful API endpoints following REST principles, HTTP standards, and resource-based URL conventions. Use this skill when creating or modifying API endpoints, routes, controllers, request handlers, or API documentation. Apply when working with REST API design, API versioning, HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE), URL structure, query parameters, response formatting, status codes, rate limiting, or API middleware. Use when building web services, microservices, or any backend code that exposes HTTP endpoints for client consumption.
skill.summary: Guide REST endpoint design, HTTP semantics, middleware planning, and API documentation.
skill.author: EIS-ITS

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent REST APIs with clear resources, methods, status codes, and documentation. This skill guides endpoint design, middleware planning, API changes, and OpenAPI documentation.
actual_capabilities: Design resource-based routes and URL structures for REST endpoints.
Choose HTTP methods and status codes for common API operations.
Plan query parameters for filtering, sorting, and pagination.
Guide middleware choices for authentication, rate limiting, and validation.
Support API documentation and OpenAPI or Swagger specification work.
Refactor endpoint structures for consistency with REST principles.
limitations: It gives guidance only; it does not generate a complete backend service alone.
It does not include framework-specific adapters or runtime code.
The current skill references a standards file outside its package.
It does not test endpoint behavior or security controls automatically.

use_cases.title: Plan a New REST Resource
use_cases.description: Define routes, methods, request expectations, status codes, and response behavior before implementation.

use_cases.title: Review Endpoint Consistency
use_cases.description: Check existing routes for naming, versioning, method usage, pagination, and error response alignment.

use_cases.title: Draft API Documentation
use_cases.description: Turn endpoint decisions into clear documentation for consumers and OpenAPI specification work.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a REST endpoint for [resource]. Include the URL, HTTP method, request data, status codes, and response shape in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Add Filtering and Pagination
prompt_templates.prompt: Design list endpoints for [resource] with filtering, sorting, and pagination. Explain query parameters, defaults, limits, and response metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Middleware and Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this API flow for authentication, authorization, validation, rate limits, and error responses. Suggest consistent middleware behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review Versioning Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this API versioning and route structure for long-term compatibility. Identify breaking changes, migration risks, and documentation needs.

output_examples.input: Design an endpoint for listing orders with pagination.
output_examples.output: Recommended route: GET /orders. Use page and limit query parameters, return a paginated order list, and use 200 for successful retrieval.

output_examples.input: Review a user update route that uses POST /updateUser.
output_examples.output: Prefer PATCH /users/{userId} for partial updates. Document validation failures, authorization failures, and the successful update response.

output_examples.input: Plan middleware for a public API endpoint.
output_examples.output: Apply authentication where needed, validate request shape, enforce rate limits, and return consistent error responses for rejected requests.

best_practices: Keep resources as nouns and reserve verbs for actions that do not map to standard methods.
Document status codes, error formats, pagination behavior, and rate limit headers with each endpoint.
Validate authentication, authorization, request shape, and idempotency decisions before implementation.
anti_patterns: Mixing action names into every URL instead of using HTTP methods.
Returning one generic status code for success, validation failures, and authorization failures.
Creating undocumented query parameters or response fields that clients must infer.

faq.question: Does this skill write backend code?
faq.answer: It guides endpoint design and implementation decisions. The final code still depends on your framework and project structure.

faq.question: Can it help with OpenAPI documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports documentation work by clarifying routes, request data, responses, status codes, and API behavior.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it cover authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for middleware planning, including authentication, rate limiting, and request validation.

faq.question: Is it limited to REST APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions focus on RESTful resources, HTTP methods, URL structure, and status codes.

faq.question: Does it validate live endpoints?
faq.answer: No. Use your test suite, API client, or monitoring tools to verify live behavior.
